research_page.title: Sabirnetug in early AD (INTERCEPT-AD Phase 1)
research_page.description: A Phase 1 first-in-human trial showing sabirnetug (ACU193) was generally well-tolerated with central target engagement and unexpected plaque reduction.
research_page.source_line_md: **Source**: [The Journal of Prevention of Alzheimer's Disease, 2024](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tjpad.2024.100005) · [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39800458/)
research_page.takeaway_md: In this Phase 1 safety study, the Aβ oligomer-targeting antibody sabirnetug demonstrated dose-dependent target engagement in the cerebrospinal fluid. The drug was generally well-tolerated with a 10.4% ARIA-E rate, but it also produced unexpected reductions in amyloid plaque despite being designed to selectively spare plaques.
key_findings_md: ARIA-E occurred in 10.4% (5 of 48) of treated participants and was mostly asymptomatic (paper, Results).
Zero cases of ARIA-E were observed in APOE ε4 homozygotes, though this subgroup contained only 6 participants (paper, Results).
High doses produced an approximate 20–25% reduction in amyloid plaque load on PET scans over three months, an unexpected finding for an oligomer-selective antibody (paper, Results).
Target engagement (sabirnetug-AβO complex) in CSF approached maximal response at 60 mg/kg every four weeks and 25 mg/kg every two weeks (paper, Results).
research_page.methods_md: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, ascending-dose Phase 1 trial ([NCT04931459](/trials/sabirnetug-nct04931459)) in 65 adults (aged 55–90) with mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia due to AD. Participants received either a single dose with 20-week follow-up or three doses over 8–12 weeks.
research_page.trial_evidence_md: This paper establishes the initial clinical evidence for sabirnetug via the Phase 1 [INTERCEPT-AD](/trials/sabirnetug-nct04931459) trial. While the trial verified safety and target engagement, it was not powered to test clinical efficacy, and PET/cognitive measures were not pre-specified endpoints in the trial registry. Disease-modifying efficacy is currently being evaluated in the fully powered Phase 2 [ALTITUDE-AD](/trials/sabirnetug-nct06335173) trial, expected to read out in late 2026.
research_page.sentiment_md: Public perception is largely hopeful among patient communities and highly enthusiastic among retail investors, who view the drug as a 'next-generation' targeted therapy. However, this hype has generated online misinformation—specifically overstating the drug's safety in APOE ε4 homozygotes based on a six-person sample, and incorrectly claiming it entirely ignores amyloid plaques despite Phase 1 PET data showing significant plaque reduction.
caveats_md: The study was sponsored, designed, and analyzed entirely by Acumen Pharmaceuticals employees, directly contradicting the paper's formal 'None' declaration for competing interests.
Amyloid plaque reduction and cognitive outcomes are emphasized in the text but were not pre-specified as primary or secondary endpoints in the official trial registry.
The claim that APOE ε4 homozygotes are protected from ARIA-E relies on a subsample of only six participants, which is statistically insufficient for broad safety generalizations.
relates_to_md: [Amyloid hypothesis](/research/amyloid-hypothesis) — The biological mechanism underlying sabirnetug's targeting of Aβ oligomers.
[Aducanumab EMERGE/ENGAGE](/research/papers/aria-aducanumab-emerge-engage) — Context for ARIA-E rates and mechanisms of action in early anti-amyloid monoclonal antibodies.

trial_pages.title: INTERCEPT-AD
trial_pages.description: Phase 1 safety and target-engagement study of intravenous sabirnetug in early Alzheimer's disease.
trial_pages.population: Adults aged 55 to 90 years with mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia due to Alzheimer's disease
trial_pages.primary_endpoint: Incidence of treatment-related adverse events and clinically significant safety changes
trial_pages.why_md: This first-in-human trial assessed whether sabirnetug, an antibody designed to selectively target toxic [amyloid-beta oligomers](/research/amyloid-hypothesis), is safe, tolerable, and successfully engages its target in the central nervous system.
trial_pages.results_md: Sabirnetug was generally well-tolerated with an overall ARIA-E rate of 10.4%. The drug demonstrated dose-dependent central target engagement of Aβ oligomers in cerebrospinal fluid and produced unexpected reductions in amyloid plaque load on PET imaging, supporting progression to Phase 2.

trial_pages.title: ALTITUDE-AD
trial_pages.description: Phase 2 efficacy and safety study of sabirnetug in early Alzheimer's disease.
trial_pages.population: Adults aged 50 to 90 years with early Alzheimer's disease and evidence of cerebral amyloid accumulation
trial_pages.primary_endpoint: Change from Baseline in Integrated Alzheimer's Disease Rating Scale (iADRS) Score
trial_pages.why_md: This trial evaluates whether specifically targeting [amyloid-beta oligomers](/research/amyloid-hypothesis) with sabirnetug can slow clinical and cognitive decline in early Alzheimer's disease.

notes_for_editor: The publication year is listed as 2024 in the DOI and article header, but the PubMed Epub date provided by the researcher is January 1, 2025. You may want to standardize how year-boundary publishing is handled.

The authors list and affiliations are completely missing from the provided source text, making the `authors_line_md` attribution difficult. I reverted to naming the sponsor (Acumen Pharmaceuticals) as the authoring entity.
